name: Gulfstream Phase IV Bartow Lateral

values.StartLocation: Tampa Bay (hot tap on Gulfstream 36-inch line)

researcher_notes: Gulfstream Pipeline Phase 4 (Bartow), EIA August 2026 release, sheet Historical Projects, Excel row 565: New expansion, completed December 2008, AL and FL, cost 117 million dollars, 17.8 miles, 155 million cubic feet per day, 20 inch, FERC docket CP07-51. An Industrial Info article says the project adds 17.5 miles of new 20 inch pipe in Manatee and Pinellas Counties plus compression, and gives the 117 million dollar cost and 155 million cubic feet per day. A Natural Gas Intelligence item on the FERC environmental review says 17.7 miles of 20 inch pipe from a hot tap on the existing 36 inch line in Tampa Bay waters to the Bartow power plant in Pinellas County. Length figures differ slightly (17.5 to 17.8 miles); staged EIA's 17.8, all above the 15.5 mile threshold (about 28 km). It is new pipe, not a loop or replacement. No existing GEM row covers it: the roster has only the whole Gulfstream system and the Phase VI row. Owners are the current parents of the Gulfstream joint venture, written as on the roster (Enbridge took over Spectra's half). Operating date inferred from EIA completion date Dec 2008. Route not researched; mostly offshore in Tampa Bay, no official GIS found. Three sources but EIA, the press piece and the NGI item all draw on the FERC filing, so independence is limited. Not checked: the FERC order itself.
